content:
Meta recently quietly launched a new application on the iPhone, using artificial intelligence to create customized stories for children, complete with illustrations, narration and original music.

This application is called "StoryKit: personalized stories". It appears to be an experimental app, as it is currently only available on the Mexican App Store and has not yet been released in the United States.

The limited availability means Meta is testing the concept in specific regions before deciding whether to roll it out more broadly.

StoryKit boasts that with just three choices, a complete story can be generated.

Users can create or take photos of characters, then choose a scene, such as a magical forest or a distant galaxy, and then pick a theme, such as values like kindness, courage or empathy.

Meta says StoryKit can then present the story in several different formats:

  • Picture book – you can swipe to turn pages, with narration and background music
  • Audiobook – hands-free, no need to look at the screen, suitable for listening while commuting, showering or before bed
  • Read aloud – displays the full text on the phone so you can be the storyteller yourself
  • Printable PDF – a physical keepsake that they can doodle on, hug while sleeping with it under their pillow, or take to share with friends

As this experiment launches, Meta has been expanding its AI ambitions beyond traditional chatbots. Earlier this year, the company replaced the Llama model with Muse Spark, which is the first model released by Meta's Superintelligence Lab.

Meta subsequently added features powered by Muse Spark to its standalone Meta AI app. Muse Spark also powers features on platforms such as WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Messenger and Threads.

However, not every synergy idea has been well received by users.

9to5Mac Perspective

StoryKit sounds like a perfectly reasonable application that, if it came from a company other than Meta, would likely be very well received.
